ajanta.description: Caves arranged in a horseshoe-shaped gorge along the Waghur River. Walking order follows cave numbering from the entrance.

walking_order.reason: Masterpiece Padmapani and Vajrapani murals
Best-preserved painted ceilings and birth of Buddha scenes
Early chaitya hall with horseshoe-shaped entrance
Oldest surviving cave, earliest Brahmi inscriptions
Famous Dying Princess mural and Conversion of Nanda
Richest repository of Jataka tale paintings
Ornate chaitya facade with Buddha figures
Majestic 7m reclining Buddha in Mahaparinirvana pose

ajanta.notes: Walking order follows the horseshoe path by cave number. Minutes and stars are editorial estimates by the student, not ASI data. Criteria for stars: significance of murals/sculptures, historical importance, visual impact for school students.

ellora.description: Caves arranged along a basalt escarpment running roughly south to north: Buddhist (1-12) → Hindu (13-29) → Jain (30-34).

walking_order.reason: Largest Buddhist vihara with stone benches
Vishwakarma Carpenter's Cave, cathedral chaitya hall
Three-storied Tin Thal vihara
Transitional Buddhist-Hindu cave
Dashavatara: Ten Incarnations of Vishnu panels
Monolithic Kailasa Temple, world's largest rock-cut monument
Rameshvara, exquisite Ganga and Yamuna sculptures
Dhumar Lena, Ravana shaking Mount Kailasa panel
Chhota Kailasa, miniature version of Cave 16
Indra Sabha, finest Jain cave with lotus ceiling
Jagannatha Sabha with Tirthankara iconography
Final cave, culmination of Ellora's three religions

ellora.notes: Walking order follows the escarpment path Buddhist → Hindu → Jain. Minutes and stars are editorial estimates by the student, not ASI data. Criteria for stars: architectural grandeur, educational value for school groups, representation of the three religions.
